thesis: The speaker argues that public markets have experienced significant dislocations between fundamental values and stock prices over the last five years because over 90% of trading activity now comes from non-fundamental sources like passive and quantitative investors rather than discretionary managers. In contrast, private markets have not faced this specific issue, though they are subject to other challenges, and the ability for companies to achieve large scale without going public has fundamentally changed the landscape of capital markets.
